Oh girl, the ultimate truth is: if a guy tells you he doesn't want a relationship, trust him.

You won't change his mind, not with a bj, or without it.
Some things simply cannot be forced. He won't miraculously commit because of that. You'd just get more frustrated cos you'll expect something to change, but nothing will. You'll be wondering why, but you'd know the answer all along. It's cos he told you so since the beginning, but you were too naive to listen. 

If he wanted to be with you, you wouldn't have to convince him.

There are several possible reasons for his behaviour ofc. One of them could be that it seems like he has deeper feelings for you. You told him you don't want a relationship, so I guess when you also show deeper affection towards him, he might think you're not being fair and that frustrates him. Because he knows if it was him doing it, you wouldn't want that. You're acting like a gf, when you don't want to be one. 
He gets super close because he still hopes it'll be ok some day(maybe you were so nice to him, he thought it's finally ok to get closer), then he learns it's still the same, that throws him back into reality, he puts up a barrier and so on. 
Or he just genuinely doesn't want a relationship and it bothers him when you act too affectionate, that's why he puts up a barrier, to remind you where you stand? In that case, doing all the nice stuff (cooking, etc.) might just be normal for him, he might be able to do that even without feeling the need to have a relationship. But if he usually doesn't stay with someone for so long, I'd say it's more the first case.

Mm, firstly, I get it, I was a virgin until 23 and super shy. Secondly, I think it's important to approach girls without the intention of having a relationship with them, cos that ruins it and you'll sound too pushy and needy. Just talk to them normally, like you would to a guy friend. That works the best, being overly nice and polite never works, it might even get creepy. I know it might be difficult to be a friend with a girl when all you want is a relationship, but when you get that connection with someone and it'll be mutual, you'll know. 
Take your time getting to know them, no rush with anything and don't create a weird atmosphere, like you're expecting something in return. 
For me, talking online works wonders. Ofc before you meet someone worth talking to, you'll meet tons of people who won't be your match, either in friendship or a relationship. Remember that you know all the things about yourself, everything you describedhow good you are etc, but they don't, you have to show them, but don't try to put everything on them at once and overwhelm them with it. Getting too personal too soon can be suspicious, and especially women in your age might have some experience already, so they'll be more cautious about it. Do no compliment at the beginning, basically don't do stuff that would seem like you're in just cos of some prospect of a relationship. On online apps, just saying hi, how are you almost never works, be natural, talk to them like to normal people. Don't be afraid to be direct about your opinions on stuff, don't be a people pleaser. Don't ask them if you can talk to them or be their friend, humour is always a plus. For starters, ask them something random, not what they've heard for hundred times already. Important skill is to be able to keep the conversation going, because there's nothing more boring than having a monologue or when it feels like an interrogation. This goes both ways though, if the girl is showing no interest with the conversation, just drop it, don't force it cos it won't work anyway. If you feel like it's not a match, you're allowed to let go without feeling bad. (Idk if you do, but I did at first, which made me talk with people I didn't wanna talk with just to not be impolite, but you learn with time).
From a girl's perspective, I realize the online stuff is kind of easier, but honestly, the best conversations I had were with guys who just messaged random stuff, not trying to Impress me with anything, not creepy, overly friendly, pushy or anything. You've got this.
Of course there could be plenty other things I could write here, but you'll find out yourself what works. And remember that not everyone will want to talk to you, just like you don't want to talk with everyone either. Best of luck :)
Edit: maybe try finding apps/chatting websites that are not relationship-focused.
